papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for large-scale knowledge discovery highlights advancements in hybrid models that integrate deep learning with structured ontology for improved knowledge extraction and document classification, particularly in biomedical literature. However, challenges such as computational expense, low interpretability, and limited applicability across domains persist. Additionally, the integration of machine learning in materials science, specifically glass design, underscores the need for predictive models that bridge theoretical and practical applications, indicating a broader potential for GNNs in scientific literature analysis.
scholarly_positioning: While prior research has made significant strides in utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for knowledge extraction and document classification, particularly in biomedical literature, these approaches often grapple with limitations such as high computational costs and low interpretability. Existing models frequently fail to fully exploit document structure and contextual information, leading to inefficiencies in knowledge discovery. Moreover, the applicability of these methods across diverse scientific domains remains underexplored. This proposed research aims to address these unresolved tensions by developing a novel GNN framework that integrates hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models, enhancing both interpretability and efficiency in large-scale knowledge discovery across various fields of scientific literature.
research_scope: This study will investigate the effectiveness of a novel hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework that integrates hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models for knowledge extraction and document classification in scientific literature, focusing on biomedical research articles. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the model's performance will be compared against existing GNN models and traditional document classification methods. Primary outcomes will include the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), F1 score, and precision and recall metrics, while secondary outcomes will assess the interpretability of the model through output-level explanation techniques and representation-level method comparisons. The target population will consist of a diverse set of biomedical literature datasets to ensure generalizability across various research domains.
concept_definition:
{
  "Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)": "A type of neural network designed to process data structured as graphs, enabling the extraction of relationships and features from nodes and edges.",
  "Hierarchical Attention Mechanisms": "A method that allows the model to focus on different levels of information (e.g., sentence, paragraph) within documents, enhancing the relevance of the features extracted.",
  "Structured Ontology Models": "Frameworks that represent knowledge in a structured way, allowing the GNN to leverage domain-specific relationships and concepts for improved understanding and classification.",
  "Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)": "A metric used to evaluate the performance of binary classification models, taking into account true and false positives and negatives, providing a balanced measure even with imbalanced datasets.",
  "F1 Score": "A measure of a model's accuracy that considers both precision and recall, providing a single score that balances the trade-off between the two.",
  "Precision": "The ratio of true positive predictions to the total predicted positives, indicating the accuracy of the positive predictions made by the model.",
  "Recall": "The ratio of true positive predictions to the total actual positives, indicating the model's ability to identify all relevant instances.",
  "Ablation Studies": "Experiments designed to evaluate the contribution of individual components of a model by systematically removing them and observing changes in performance.",
  "Output-Level Explanation Techniques": "Methods that provide insights into the model's predictions by explaining the final outputs, often aimed at users or researchers for understanding decision-making.",
  "Representation-Level Method Comparisons": "Comparative analysis of different techniques used to represent data within the model, focusing on how these representations affect interpretability and performance.",
  "Baseline Comparisons": "Evaluating the proposed model against existing models and traditional methods to establish a performance benchmark.",
  "Interpretability": "The degree to which a human can understand the cause of a decision made by a model, often assessed through specific techniques like attention visualization or attribution methods.",
  "User Trust": "The confidence users have in the model's predictions, which can be influenced by perceived transparency, trust calibration, and the reliability of the model's explanations."
}
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible but requires access to open-source GNN models for implementation and experimentation. It will also need labeled datasets of biomedical literature for training and evaluation, as well as GPU resources for model training. Since the study involves interpretability and user trust, it may require a human-subject design to assess user trust in the model's predictions, necessitating ethics approval. If internal representations are to be studied, access to hidden states of the GNN would be beneficial. A feasible adjustment would be to focus on output-level explanation techniques if hidden-state access is not available.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in knowledge extraction within biomedical literature; however, they treat the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models as secondary, leaving unclear whether these enhancements significantly improve interpretability and efficiency in broader scientific contexts. This matters theoretically because it limits the understanding of GNN applicability across diverse domains and practically because it hinders the development of more robust knowledge discovery tools. Therefore, this study investigates the impact of integrating hierarchical attention and structured ontology models within a GNN framework on knowledge extraction and document classification across various scientific literature domains.
question: How does the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models within a Graph Neural Network framework impact knowledge extraction and document classification accuracy in biomedical literature compared to traditional document classification methods?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models (independent variable) within a Graph Neural Network framework, aiming to enhance knowledge extraction and document classification accuracy (dependent variable) in biomedical literature. The hierarchical attention mechanism serves as a mediator by improving the model's focus on relevant document features, while the structured ontology model acts as a moderator, facilitating the understanding of domain-specific relationships. This integration is grounded in the theoretical framework of interpretability in machine learning, suggesting that better feature extraction leads to improved model performance. System-level outcomes include increased classification accuracy and efficiency, while user-level outcomes involve enhanced perceived transparency and satisfaction with the model's predictions. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of attention mechanisms in improving feature relevance and the impact of structured ontologies on model interpretability.
hypothesis: The integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models within a Graph Neural Network framework will significantly improve document classification accuracy, as measured by the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), compared to traditional document classification methods, with the hierarchical attention mechanism enhancing the relevance of extracted features.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework that integrates hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models to enhance knowledge extraction and document classification in biomedical literature. Key concepts include GNNs, which process graph-structured data; hierarchical attention mechanisms that improve feature relevance by focusing on critical document features; and structured ontology models that facilitate domain-specific understanding of relationships. The study is technically feasible, requiring access to open-source GNN models, labeled biomedical datasets, and GPU resources for training. The motivation stems from existing GNN applications that struggle with high computational costs and low interpretability, particularly in their failure to leverage document structure and contextual information. The scholarly positioning highlights that while prior research has made strides in GNN applications, they often do not fully exploit hierarchical attention and structured ontology integration, leading to a gap in empirical validation of these enhancements across diverse scientific domains. The research question is: How does the integration of hierarchical attention mechanisms and structured ontology models within a GNN framework impact knowledge extraction and document classification accuracy in biomedical literature compared to traditional document classification methods? The theoretical mechanism posits that the hierarchical attention mechanism mediates improved feature relevance, while the structured ontology model moderates the understanding of domain-specific relationships, leading to enhanced knowledge extraction and classification accuracy. The hypothesis is that the proposed GNN framework will significantly improve document classification accuracy, as measured by the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), compared to traditional methods. Constructs will be operationalized using metrics such as MCC, F1 score, precision, and recall for knowledge extraction and classification accuracy, with interpretability assessed through output-level explanation techniques and user trust measured via trust calibration surveys. The methodology includes ablation studies to isolate the effects of the integrated mechanisms, with controls for dataset quality and model training variability. Expected contributions encompass theoretical advancements in GNN frameworks, technical innovations in hybrid model design, empirical validation through performance metrics, and practical guidelines for enhancing user trust and interpretability in biomedical research applications. Key limitations include potential confounding variables, dataset quality variability, and the inability to generalize findings beyond biomedical literature without further research.
